content.content: 1 # Meeting-room booking app — full spec (verbatim from the user; final, no questions possible) 2 3 Constraints: Node.js built-ins only (no npm install). Node v22. Project tests must pass at the end. 4 5 Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. 6 7 ## Server 8 - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. 9 - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 10 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 11 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 12 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 13 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 14 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 15 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. 16 - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. 17 - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. 18 19 ## API 20 - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 21 - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. 22 - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. 23 - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. 24 - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. 25 - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. 26 - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. 27 - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. 28 - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). 29 - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. This includes every path that starts with `/api/bookings/` and whose rest is empty or holds a `/`, such as `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`. 30 - A path above with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked. 31 - Every reply with a body other than the page and the script has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": ""}` with exactly that key, where `` is the text given here. 32 33 ## Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`; the first rule that fails decides the reply) 34 1. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 35 2. The body is longer than 10000 bytes, counting the body bytes actually received: 413 `body too large`. 36 3. The body, decoded as `Buffer.prototype.toString('utf8')` does and then given to `JSON.parse`, is not a JSON object (it is empty, not valid JSON, `null`, an array, a string, a number or a boolean): 400 `body must be a JSON object`. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD and are not an error by themselves. A byte order mark at the very start is kept, so such a body is not valid JSON. 37 4. `room` is not a string equal to one of the room names (letter case matters): 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`. 38 5. `title` is not a string, or is shorter than 1 or longer than 80 UTF-16 code units after removing the whitespace at both ends (as `String.prototype.trim` does): 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters`. The booking keeps the trimmed title. 39 6. `date` is not a string `YYYY-MM-DD` (4, 2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) naming a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31, where February has 29 days in years divisible by 4: 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. 40 7. `start` is not a string `HH:MM` (2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) from `00:00` to `23:59`: 400 `start must be HH:MM`. 41 8. `end` is not such a string: 400 `end must be HH:MM`. 42 9. `end` is not later than `start`: 400 `end must be after start`. 43 10. The booking overlaps a booking of the same room on the same date, that is each of the two starts before the other ends (a booking may start exactly when another ends): 409 `room is already booked from to `, with the start and end of the overlapping booking that starts earliest. 44 - No field except `title` is trimmed or changed: ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and `9:00` are invalid. 45 46 ## Page 47 - `GET /` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8` and the page. `GET /app.js` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/javascript; charset=utf-8` and the page's script. 48 - The page loads the script with a `

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 600000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

content.text: I graded `public/index.html` (53 lines) and `public/app.js` (182 lines) against every line of the spec's "## Page" section. Both files pass: overall 8/10, no item under 6. The repo has no CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or `.claude/rules` file, so only the house rules and the spec applied. I read the files but ran nothing, since tests are n/a. **The spec checks all pass** - **Ids, attributes and text:** all match. The form has `novalidate`, the five fields have the right types and names, `Book` is `type="submit"`, and each label (including `Show date`) sits beside its field rather than wrapping it. `#filter-date`, `#show-all`, `#booking-list` and `#error` are outside the form, and `#error` is empty. The `` and the single `<h1>` both read `Room bookings`. - **Nothing forbidden in the HTML:** no `<option>`, no room names, no inline script, no `on...` attributes, and no `http://` or `https://` in either file. - **Script tag:** `<script src="/app.js">` is the last element in `<body>`, with no `type`, `defer` or `async`. The script is classic, has no import or export, and starts at once with no load event. The rooms fetch and the first list fetch start together without waiting on each other. - **Browser APIs:** only the allowed ones are used. Everything else (`Array.isArray`, `JSON.stringify`, `.map`) is plain JavaScript, not a browser API. - **Plain text only:** values are shown with `textContent` and `append(string)`, never as HTML. The text line is ``${date} ${start}-${end} ${room}: ${title}`` followed by the Cancel button. An empty list gives a single `No bookings.` item. - **Requests:** - URLs are path-only. - The `?date=` value is sent unchanged. - The POST sends exactly one `Content-Type: application/json` header, with the five values untrimmed. - A 204 reply's body is not read. - A non-204 reply that isn't JSON counts as no reply. - The error message falls back to `Request failed.`. - **Behaviour:** - Overlapping list fetches are handled by a counter, so only the last one started is used. - `Book` and `Cancel` are re-enabled straight after the request settles. - A submit while `Book` is disabled sends nothing, and `preventDefault` comes first. - A failed cancel with no reply does not refetch the list. - Only the `change` event on the filter fetches; `input` does nothing. - `Show all` clears the filter and fetches once, without dispatching an event. **What costs points** 1. **Repeated reply handling.** `loadRooms` (`app.js:63-79`) and `loadList` (`app.js:109-130`) handle the reply the same way: no reply, wrong status, then pull an array out of the body. That could be one shared helper. 2. **Possible stray error.** `bookingItem` (`app.js:81-92`) assumes each booking is an object. A `null` entry in the reply would throw inside a call that nothing waits on (`loadList()` at lines 156, 168, 173, 181), so the error appears in the browser console instead of `#error`. The server controls this data, so it is a small risk. 3. **Built by mutation.** `request` (`app.js:36-40`) creates `options` and then adds fields to it, where it could build the finished object in one go. 4. **Vague name.** `mine` (`app.js:111`) would be clearer as `requestSeq` or similar. 5. **Layout filler.** `index.html:43` has an empty `<span></span>` that only fills a grid cell; CSS can do this instead. ## GRADE Overall: 8/10 Verdict: pass structure: 8 — small single-purpose functions and the last-fetch rule handled cleanly; `request` builds its options by mutation naming: 8 — clear names overall; `mine` is vague duplication: 7 — loadRooms and loadList repeat the same reply-handling steps size: 10 — 182 and 53 lines; every function well under 50 lines errors: 8 — every spec message is exact and `request` never throws; a malformed booking would throw a stray error from a fire-and-forget loadList tests: n/a — written by the testing section security: 9 — all values rendered as text, no HTML injection, path-only URLs, no secrets leftovers: 9 — no console.log or commented-out code; one empty filler `<span>` Fixes: - /root/bench-runs/h4-671cf6e0/public/app.js:63 move the shared "no reply / wrong status / get the array field" steps of loadRooms and loadList (lines 63-79 and 109-130) into one helper, e.g. `readList(reply, expectedStatus, key)` - /root/bench-runs/h4-671cf6e0/public/app.js:36 build options in one go, e.g. `payload === undefined ? { method } : { method, headers: {...}, body: JSON.stringify(payload) }`, instead of adding fields later - /root/bench-runs/h4-671cf6e0/public/app.js:124 also check that each booking is an object, or catch the rendering error, so a malformed reply shows `Request failed.` instead of a stray error - /root/bench-runs/h4-671cf6e0/public/app.js:111 rename `mine` to `requestSeq` (or similar) - /root/bench-runs/h4-671cf6e0/public/index.html:43 remove the empty `<span></span>` and place `#show-all` with CSS (e.g. `grid-column: 2`)
